projects.title: CropPulse AI: Precision Crop Recommendation
projects.tagline: Random Forest crop recommender for 22 crops with a Flask API, serverless fallback engine, and an interactive web app deployed on Vercel.
projects.summary: An end-to-end machine learning application that recommends the most suitable crop from soil nutrients (N, P, K), temperature, humidity, pH, and rainfall. Three classifiers were benchmarked on 2,200 samples across 22 crop classes; the production Random Forest reaches 99.55% test accuracy and is served through a Flask API on Vercel with a zero-dependency JSON decision-tree fallback, nutrient gap analysis, and fertilizer guidance.

metrics.subtext: Cereals, pulses, fruits, and plantation/cash crops

highlights: Benchmarked Random Forest (99.55%), Decision Tree (97.95%), and Logistic Regression (95.00%) on identical stratified splits.
Dual-engine inference: scikit-learn/joblib model plus a zero-dependency JSON decision-tree evaluator for serverless reliability.
Interactive UI with agro-ecological presets, Open-Meteo weather autofill, nutrient gap analysis, and fertilizer schedules.
REST API (/api/predict, /api/crops, /api/model-info, /api/health) covered by a 10-test automated suite.
projects.problem: Smallholder farmers often lack accessible, data-backed tools to pick the right crop for their soil NPK balance and local weather conditions.
projects.approach: Benchmarked Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest across 2,200 labeled samples (22 classes); deployed the 99.55%-accurate Random Forest behind a Flask API with Open-Meteo weather autofill and nutrient gap feedback.
projects.challenges: Heavy scikit-learn dependencies can trigger cold-start timeouts on serverless deployments, so I implemented a zero-dependency JSON decision-tree fallback engine for reliable inference on Vercel.
projects.keyArchitecture: Soil & Climate Inputs (N, P, K, Temp, Humidity, pH, Rainfall) → Flask API on Vercel → Random Forest (joblib) or JSON Tree Fallback → Crop + Confidence + Alternates → Suitability & Fertilizer Advisory UI.

projects.title: Moodline: Deep Learning Emotion Classification
projects.tagline: BiGRU-based NLP system that classifies text into six emotions, served via an async FastAPI backend and deployed on Render.
projects.summary: An end-to-end deep learning and NLP application for multi-class emotion classification (joy, sadness, love, anger, fear, surprise). Four sequence architectures — SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU, and Bidirectional GRU — were trained and compared on the Hugging Face dair-ai/emotion dataset. The best model (BiGRU, ~90.1% test accuracy) is served in real time through a FastAPI backend with an interactive web UI, Docker containerization, and an automated test suite.

highlights: Compared SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU, and BiGRU models; selected BiGRU for its bidirectional context.
Text pipeline: cleaning, contraction normalization, tokenization, and padding to 50 tokens with 300-d embeddings.
Async FastAPI service returning the predicted emotion, full probability distribution, and latency.
Dockerfile with a non-root user and health checks, a Render blueprint, and an end-to-end test suite.
projects.problem: Keyword rules struggle to capture nuanced emotional intent in short text across subtle overlapping classes like sadness, fear, and anger.
projects.approach: Built a consistent preprocessing pipeline (50-token padding, 300-d embeddings) and trained SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU, and BiGRU side-by-side on dair-ai/emotion, deploying the best BiGRU (~90.1%) in an async FastAPI + Docker service.
projects.challenges: Unidirectional RNNs missed context from trailing negation and modifiers, which bidirectional layers solved—paired with Spatial Dropout to curb overfitting on minority classes like love and surprise.
projects.keyArchitecture: Raw Text → Preprocessing & Tokenization (max len 50) → Embedding (300-d) → BiGRU (128) → Spatial Dropout → BiGRU (64) → Dropout → Softmax (6 emotions) → FastAPI /predict → Web UI.

projects.title: DocMind: Multi-PDF RAG Q&A Chatbot
projects.tagline: Retrieval-Augmented Generation assistant for chatting with multiple PDFs using LangChain, FAISS, and Llama 3.2 or GPT-3.5.
projects.summary: A conversational RAG application that lets users upload one or more PDF documents and ask natural-language questions about them. Text is extracted with PyPDF, split into overlapping chunks, embedded with sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), and indexed in an in-memory FAISS vector store. A LangChain ConversationalRetrievalChain with conversation memory generates grounded answers using either Hugging Face Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct or OpenAI GPT-3.5-Turbo, all inside a Streamlit interface.

highlights: Simultaneous multi-PDF ingestion into a single searchable knowledge base.
Dual LLM backend selectable from the sidebar: Hugging Face Inference API or OpenAI.
Conversation memory (ConversationBufferMemory) for coherent follow-up questions.
Graceful handling of scanned/empty PDFs, missing API keys, and OpenAI quota errors.
projects.problem: Reading and cross-referencing information across multiple dense PDF documents manually is slow, while prompting an LLM directly without context causes hallucinations.
projects.approach: Extracted text with PyPDF, split documents into overlapping chunks (1000/200 chars), embedded them using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 into a FAISS vector store, and built a LangChain ConversationalRetrievalChain supporting Llama 3.2 and GPT-3.5.
projects.challenges: Tuned chunk boundaries so multi-paragraph context remained intact during similarity lookup, and added explicit error handling for scanned PDFs with no selectable text layer.
projects.keyArchitecture: PDF Upload → PyPDF Text Extraction → CharacterTextSplitter (1000/200) → all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Embeddings → FAISS Index → Similarity Retrieval → ConversationalRetrievalChain + Memory → Llama 3.2 / GPT-3.5 → Streamlit Chat UI.

projects.title: FocusBell AI: In-Browser Phone Distraction Detector
projects.tagline: Study focus timer that uses real-time COCO-SSD object detection in TensorFlow.js to catch phone use and reset the session.
projects.summary: A productivity web app that combines a configurable focus timer with real-time computer vision running entirely in the browser. A pre-trained COCO-SSD model (TensorFlow.js) analyzes webcam frames; when a 'cell phone' is detected with confidence above 0.65 during an active session, the app plays an audio alert, shows a warning state, and resets the timer. Webcam frames are processed locally on the device.

highlights: Continuous frame-by-frame detection with requestAnimationFrame on the webcam stream.
Phone detection triggers an audio alert, a warning UI state, and a timer reset to enforce focus.
Configurable hour/minute/second timer (25-minute default) with pause, resume, and abort controls.
Deployed on Vercel as a lightweight React + Vite single-page app.
projects.problem: Standard study timers don't prevent unconscious smartphone distractions, while cloud-based webcam tools raise serious privacy concerns.
projects.approach: Integrated pre-trained COCO-SSD object detection via TensorFlow.js directly inside React so frames never leave the user's browser, alerting and resetting the study timer when a phone is detected (>0.65 confidence).
projects.challenges: Continuous detection frames caused UI jank and repeated false-trigger sounds, which I fixed using requestAnimationFrame pacing and a 4-second cooldown gate.
projects.keyArchitecture: Webcam MediaStream → HTML5 Video → COCO-SSD (TensorFlow.js) Detection Loop → 'cell phone' score > 0.65 → Cooldown Gate (4 s) → Audio Alert + Timer Reset.

research.title: AI-Based Intelligent Driving Assistance System for Bangladesh’s Unstructured & Uneven Roads
research.tagline: Perception architectures suited to non-lane traffic, pavement hazards, and mixed vehicles in South Asian driving environments.
research.targetOutcome: Undergraduate Thesis & Prospective Graduate Research Proposal
research.problem: Standard autonomous vehicle perception datasets (e.g. KITTI, Waymo, nuScenes) presume clearly delineated road lanes, uniform vehicle geometry, and orderly pedestrian crossings. In Bangladesh, roads are largely non-lane-based, dominated by heterogeneous non-motorized and three-wheeled vehicles (rickshaws, CNG auto-rickshaws), unpredictable pedestrian crossings, and severe surface degradation (potholes, unpaved shoulders).
research.researchQuestion: How can a lightweight monocular computer vision architecture jointly perceive unstructured multi-class obstacles and segment road-surface hazards under challenging visual conditions (monsoon rain glare, dust, low-light illumination) on edge compute budgets?
research.whyItMatters: Road traffic injuries are a major public-safety challenge in South Asia. Affordable, aftermarket dashcam-based assistance systems could provide proactive collision and pothole warnings without expensive sensor suites.
research.existingApproaches: Commercial systems rely heavily on lane-departure warning heuristics and LiDAR point clouds. Existing road anomaly studies typically isolate pothole detection on static frames or depend on sensor rigs tailored to structured Western roadways.
research.researchGap: Scarcity of open-access Bangladeshi multi-hazard driving datasets, limited joint perception models that operate without lane priors, and strong domain shifts across local vehicle classes and weather.
research.proposedDirection: A dual-task lightweight convolutional architecture sharing a visual backbone: one head for localized object detection and tracking (rickshaws, auto-rickshaws, buses, pedestrians) and a second head for drivable-area and pothole segmentation, paired with monocular proximity heuristics.
research.experiments: Currently in conceptual formulation and literature review stage; planned empirical work will benchmark detection mAP, segmentation IoU, and edge inference latency once a localized dashcam video benchmark is collected and annotated.
research.currentResults: Formalized the problem definition, target perception taxonomy, and architectural outline. No custom dataset collection, model training, or empirical field experiments have been conducted yet.
research.limitations: Strictly a research direction and proposal outline at this stage; requires curated, annotated field video across varied Bangladeshi traffic and weather conditions before empirical validation.
research.futureWork: Develop as an undergraduate thesis and prospective Master's research topic: curate and annotate local road footage, benchmark YOLO-family detectors on local vehicle classes, and test quantized edge deployment.
research.statusNote: Research Direction & Proposal Formulation (No empirical results claimed yet)

research.title: Comparative Sequence Modeling for Multi-Class Emotion Recognition in Text
research.tagline: Evaluating recurrent gating and bidirectional context across SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU, and BiGRU on six-class affective text.
research.targetOutcome: Deployed Inference System (Moodline) & Future Transformer / Low-Resource Extension
research.problem: Coarse binary sentiment analysis (positive vs negative) obscures distinct emotional states such as sadness, fear, and anger that carry very different meanings in user feedback, mental-health triage, and conversational agents.
research.researchQuestion: How strongly do gated recurrent units and bidirectional context improve six-class emotion discrimination on short text sequences, and where do fixed-vocabulary recurrent models break down compared to contextual transformers?
research.whyItMatters: Understanding the accuracy-latency-parameter trade-offs between lightweight recurrent models and larger pretrained transformers helps engineers deploy responsive NLP systems on constrained cloud or edge hardware.
research.existingApproaches: Bag-of-words linear baselines miss word order and negation, while large transformer encoders add higher memory and inference latency footprints in CPU-only containers.
research.researchGap: Comparing recurrent variants under identical preprocessing and deployment constraints while extending affective NLP evaluations to code-mixed and Bangla text.
research.proposedDirection: Benchmarked four recurrent architectures (SimpleRNN, LSTM, GRU, BiGRU) with 300-dimensional embeddings and SpatialDropout(0.5) on the Hugging Face dair-ai/emotion dataset, deploying the best model behind a FastAPI + Docker service.
research.experiments: Trained all four sequence models under a 50-token padded pipeline (~15,000-word vocabulary) in sentiment_analysis.ipynb and verified end-to-end API behavior through an automated 5-test suite in Moodline.
research.currentResults: Observed progressive gains from SimpleRNN (~78.4%, ~1.3M params) to LSTM (~86.2%, ~1.6M params), GRU (~87.8%, ~1.5M params), and BiGRU (~90.1%, ~2.1M params), with BiGRU served live at moodline-sentiment.onrender.com.
research.limitations: Evaluations currently report aggregate test accuracy on a single English benchmark with a 50-token window; per-class confusion breakdowns and cross-domain or Bangla generalization have not yet been benchmarked.
research.futureWork: Compare BiGRU directly against fine-tuned compact transformers (e.g. DistilBERT), add per-class F1 and calibration metrics, and extend experiments to Bangla emotion datasets.
research.statusNote: Implemented & Deployed in Moodline; Transformer Comparison Planned

research.title: Grounded Multi-Document Retrieval-Augmented Generation & Hybrid Reranking
research.tagline: Exploring chunking sensitivity, hybrid lexical-dense search, and cross-encoder reranking beyond single-stage FAISS baselines.
research.targetOutcome: Working Multi-PDF RAG Baseline (DocMind) & Two-Stage Retrieval Study
research.problem: Single-stage dense vector retrieval can return top-k chunks that are topically adjacent yet miss exact technical terms or split key facts across chunk boundaries, degrading LLM answer faithfulness.
research.researchQuestion: How do chunking boundaries, hybrid sparse-dense retrieval (BM25 + dense embeddings), and cross-encoder reranking affect retrieval precision and answer grounding compared to a single-stage FAISS baseline?
research.whyItMatters: Students, researchers, and engineers querying dense multi-PDF technical or academic corpora need verifiable, source-grounded answers rather than plausible-sounding hallucinations.
research.existingApproaches: Standard LangChain/FAISS pipelines split text into fixed-size character chunks (e.g. 1,000 characters with 200 overlap) and retrieve via cosine similarity alone without reranking or citation verification.
research.researchGap: Evaluating exact-term recall and multi-document attribution across lightweight local embedding models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) paired with small open-weights LLMs (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct).
research.proposedDirection: Built the baseline pipeline in DocMind (PyPDF + CharacterTextSplitter 1000/200 + all-MiniLM-L6-v2 + FAISS + ConversationalRetrievalChain with Llama 3.2 / GPT-3.5) and actively exploring two-stage hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense Reciprocal Rank Fusion) with cross-encoder reranking and page-level source citations.
research.experiments: Implemented and manually tested multi-PDF ingestion, conversation buffer memory, and dual Hugging Face / OpenAI LLM switching in DocMind; quantitative RAG evaluation (faithfulness and context recall benchmarks) is planned next.
research.currentResults: Working Streamlit application supporting multi-PDF upload, 384D local MiniLM embeddings, FAISS search, and graceful error handling for scanned PDFs and API limits.
research.limitations: Current implementation uses single-stage dense similarity search without reranking, stores the FAISS index in memory per session, and has not yet been evaluated on a labeled RAG benchmark.
research.futureWork: Add page-level source citations, implement BM25 + dense hybrid retrieval with a cross-encoder reranker, support OCR for scanned PDFs, and benchmark retrieval metrics systematically.
research.statusNote: Baseline Implemented in DocMind; Reranking & Evaluation Under Exploration

Shipped a dual-engine Flask API on Vercel combining scikit-learn/joblib with a 0.68 ms zero-dependency JSON decision-tree fallback and Open-Meteo autofill.
journey.keyOutcome: Practical mastery of comparative benchmarking and serverless ML serving.

journey.title: Deep Learning & NLP Sequence Modeling
journey.domain: TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch, BiGRU / LSTM, FastAPI, Docker
journey.description: Moved into deep neural sequence modeling and containerized NLP inference. Built Moodline on the Hugging Face dair-ai/emotion dataset to classify text into six emotions: joy, sadness, love, anger, fear, and surprise.
focusPoints: Trained and benchmarked SimpleRNN (~78.4%), LSTM (~86.2%), GRU (~87.8%), and Bidirectional GRU (~90.1%) with 300D embeddings and SpatialDropout.
Built an async FastAPI service with /predict and /health endpoints, Swagger/ReDoc documentation, and resilient Keras 3 deserialization.
Containerized the pipeline with Docker (non-root user, health checks), wrote a 5-test automated suite, and deployed live on Render.

journey.title: Computer Vision & In-Browser Inference
journey.description: Explored real-time visual perception directly inside the web browser without transmitting webcam video to external servers. Built FocusBell AI to pair a configurable focus timer with automated smartphone distraction detection.
focusPoints: Integrated pre-trained COCO-SSD via @tensorflow-models/coco-ssd and @tensorflow/tfjs on a 640×480 webcam MediaStream.
Implemented continuous requestAnimationFrame inference filtering for 'cell phone' detections above 0.65 confidence.
Added a 4-second alert cooldown, audio alert feedback, and automatic session reset, deployed on Vercel.

journey.domain: Llama 3.2, OpenAI GPT-3.5, Hugging Face, Sentence-Transformers

Integrated dual inference providers: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct via Hugging Face Inference API and OpenAI gpt-3.5-turbo.
Handled edge cases gracefully, including missing API credentials, quota exhaustion fallbacks, and unextractable scanned PDFs.

journey.description: Built DocMind for conversational Q&A over multiple uploaded PDFs using LangChain and FAISS, while actively studying advanced RAG techniques — hybrid sparse-dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and agentic tool-use workflows.
focusPoints: Implemented multi-PDF ingestion with PyPDF, CharacterTextSplitter (1000 chars, 200 overlap), FAISS indexing, and ConversationBufferMemory.
Studying Reciprocal Rank Fusion (BM25 + dense embeddings) and cross-encoder reranking to reduce noisy context chunks.
Exploring structured agentic patterns including ReAct tool calling and verification loops.
